claims.text: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) has an unmodified alpha-plus-beta dual-phase microstructure.
Untreated TC4 has relatively low surface hardness and poor tribological performance.
Untreated TC4 has desirable bulk ductility and fatigue resistance.
Plasma nitriding TC4 at 550 degrees Celsius for 4 hours will produce a nitrogen-enriched surface layer.
The treatment will form fine TiN precipitates in the TC4 surface.
Nitrogen diffuses into the TC4 surface during plasma nitriding.
The TiN precipitates will be uniformly dispersed and embedded in the titanium matrix.
Interstitial nitrogen will provide solid-solution strengthening.
TiN formation and interstitial solid-solution strengthening will increase surface hardness.
TiN formation and interstitial solid-solution strengthening will improve wear resistance.
The underlying alpha-plus-beta microstructure will remain largely unaltered after treatment.
Controlled cooling will minimize thermal stresses and preserve the bulk microstructure.
Plasma nitriding will increase TC4 surface hardness by 50–100% relative to untreated TC4.
Plasma nitriding will significantly reduce TC4 wear rate relative to untreated TC4.
The treatment will maintain TC4 bulk fatigue resistance.
The treatment will maintain TC4 bulk ductility.
The predicted improvements apply under moderate thermal and mechanical stresses.
Treatment variability and precipitate-distribution homogeneity can influence the magnitude of improvement.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts both increased hardness and reduced wear, but the falsification rule joins their failure with 'and,' potentially allowing failure of one required outcome without falsifying the hypothesis. The phrase describing 'less than 20% improvement' as an example associated with a statistically significant wear reduction is also logically ambiguous.
